quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
quiz_item.question: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
options: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
choices: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): AI and machine learning systems infer patterns directly from training data sets; if the training data contains gaps or historical biases, the resulting model outputs will reflect those flaws, requiring human verification.

requirements.description: Career Exploration. Do ONE of the following: (a) Identify three career opportunities that would use skills and knowledge in artificial intelligence or automation. Pick one and research the training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities, and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career. (b) Interview an artificial intelligence or automation professional. Learn about their day-to-day work, the challenges they face, and their vision for the future of artificial intelligence or automation. Inquire about training, education, certification requirements, experience, and expenses associated with entering the field. Share what you learned with your counselor.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When evaluating how a machine learning model makes predictions in Artificial Intelligence Requirement 1, why can an AI system produce biased or inaccurate outputs even when its software code has no syntax errors?
options: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
choices: A. Because machine learning algorithms physically wear out their silicon transistors after processing more than a thousand queries.
B. Because AI models never use training data and instead generate answers using purely random voltage fluctuations.
C. Because computer processors automatically rewrite their own operating systems to ignore human instructions after compilation.

D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from their training data, so unrepresentative, incomplete, or historically skewed data will cause the model to reproduce those biases and errors.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): AI and machine learning systems infer patterns directly from training data sets; if the training data contains gaps or historical biases, the resulting model outputs will reflect those flaws, requiring human verification.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: During the 'AI or Not?' game with your counselor, which of the following everyday scenarios actually utilizes artificial intelligence?
options: A. A digital kitchen timer beeping when sixty seconds have elapsed
B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
C. An automatic sliding grocery store door opening when a motion sensor beam is broken
D. A word processor alphabetizing a list of Scout names from A to Z
choices: A. A digital kitchen timer beeping when sixty seconds have elapsed
B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
C. An automatic sliding grocery store door opening when a motion sensor beam is broken
D. A word processor alphabetizing a list of Scout names from A to Z
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. A smartphone camera recognizing a user's face under different lighting angles to unlock the screen
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Facial recognition uses trained machine learning models to identify features across varying lighting and angles, whereas timers, basic motion sensors, and alphabetical sorting use fixed rules (p. 6).

D. It replaces structured databases with unorganized text files.
choices: A. It performs repetitive steps without human intervention, reducing human error and optimizing resources.
B. It enables the machine to invent brand-new business goals without human oversight.

D. It replaces structured databases with unorganized text files.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It performs repetitive steps without human intervention, reducing human error and optimizing resources.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Automation executes repetitive workflows consistently without continuous human intervention, which minimizes human error and optimizes time, energy, and material resources (p. 6).

options: A. Whether a computer's power supply can run for twenty-four hours without overheating
B. Whether a database can encrypt ten million passwords in under one second
C. Whether a robot arm can lift heavier loads than a human factory worker
D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
choices: A. Whether a computer's power supply can run for twenty-four hours without overheating
B. Whether a database can encrypt ten million passwords in under one second
C. Whether a robot arm can lift heavier loads than a human factory worker
D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Whether a machine can generate text responses in a conversation that a human judge cannot distinguish from another human
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The Turing test evaluates whether a machine can communicate in natural language convincingly enough that an evaluator cannot reliably tell the machine apart from a human (p. 6).
